item.title: US, Japan defence chiefs agree China harming regional peace
item.description: By Hiroshi Hiyama Beijing’s actions are “not conducive to regional peace”, Japan’s defence minister and US counterpart Pete Hegseth agreed during a call after Chinese aircraft locked radar on Japanese jets near Taiwan, Tokyo said Friday. item.title: Domestic worker injured in Tai Po fire returns to Philippines after hospital discharge
item.description: A Filipina domestic worker caught in the fatal Tai Po fire a day after arriving in the city has been discharged from hospital and will be returning home, according to an NGO. item.title: Judge David Lok to lead Tai Po fire review committee; probe due in 9 months
item.description: High Court Judge David Lok, who also heads the Hong Kong Electoral Affairs Commission, will chair the independent review committee investigating the deadly Tai Po fire. Chief Executive John Lee announced Lok’s appointment on Friday, more than a week after ordering the establishment of a judge-led committee to probe the blaze, which killed at least […]

item.title: Hong Kong national security police arrest 9 men for alleged military-style ‘unlawful drills’
item.description: Hong Kong national security police have arrested nine men for allegedly engaging in “unlawful drills” involving military-style firearms and combat training. The nine suspects, aged 20 to 25, were arrested on Thursday night, police said on Friday. Authorities invoked the “illegal drilling” provision under the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, Hong Kong’s homegrown security law also […]

item.title: HKFP Monitor Dec 13, 2025: How Hong Kong mourned Tai Po fire victims; new ‘all patriots’ legislature
item.description: This week, we round up the different ways Hong Kong grieved for the victims of the deadly Tai Po fire, which has claimed at least 160 lives. item.description: Flipping and spinning on a studio floor, 17-year-old Royal is a star in China’s breakdancing scene and aiming for gold at the World Championships in Japan this week. item.title: EU agrees three-euro small parcel tax to tackle China flood
item.description: EU finance ministers agreed Friday to impose a three-euro duty on all small parcels imported into the bloc starting July 1, 2026, to help tackle a flood of cheap imports by the likes of Shein and Temu. item.title: Exhibition of Franco-Chinese print master Zao Wou-Ki opens in Hong Kong
item.description: An exhibition by the Franco-Chinese artist Zao Wou-Ki opened in Hong Kong on Saturday, the first time his print work has been on display in Asia. item.description: In November, Hong Kong’s national security police made several arrests related to the fatal blaze that tore through a housing estate in Tai Po and the “patriots only” Legislative Council (LegCo) elections. item.title: China defends jailing Chinese-Swedish bookseller Gui Minhai after UN group urges release
item.description: China rejected on Thursday any “interference” in its judicial sovereignty after a United Nations working group called for the immediate release of jailed Chinese-Swedish bookseller Gui Minhai.
